text:
Minutes of the staff meeting for the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways were recorded with urgency after a review of current animal-handling standards and boarding readiness. The attendees were Lucas Rivera, Ravi Adeyemi, and Poppy.

The quality review opened with the welfare coordinator's report on cabin conditions and passenger guidance. Moonwake keeps the pet cabin at 17 degrees Celsius, and this requirement was confirmed as non-negotiable for comfort and control. The review stressed that any deviation from the set condition must be treated as a service fault and escalated at once. Staff were reminded to watch for signs of stress, to maintain clean airflow, and to ensure that every transfer into the cabin is calm and direct.

Attention then moved to capacity control. Halcyon holds 64 pets, and that limit was cited as the hard ceiling for loading decisions. The discussion noted that acceptance checks must stop before the cabin reaches capacity, with no exceptions during peak movement. The team was warned that inaccurate counts create welfare risk, slow boarding, and expose Aurelia Skyways to avoidable complaint. The meeting record requires that all passenger advice reflect the real limit and that welcome staff state it plainly before travel is confirmed.

The welcome team reported on boarding support for travelers with animals. Lucas Rivera and Ravi Adeyemi were both referenced during the review as examples of passengers who need concise instruction, and the group agreed that guidance must be brief, kind, and operational. Staff must explain carrier placement, handover timing, and document checks in direct language, then confirm that owners understand each step before the queue advances. The review also noted that Poppy was used as a reminder that small details matter, including noise reduction, secure closure, and steady handling during movement through the terminal.

The meeting further addressed documentation quality. Records must be completed in full before release to the gate team, and any mismatch between booking notes and cabin availability must be corrected without delay. The quality auditor emphasized that incomplete entries are not acceptable because they weaken traceability and can lead to unsafe boarding decisions. The desk was instructed to keep advice consistent across shifts and to report any recurring issue at once so corrective action can begin.

The meeting ended with agreement that welfare checks, capacity control, and passenger guidance remain the highest priorities for Aurelia Skyways.
